findings.note: No P1 findings. The delta is correctly scoped: path.normalize is applied only at the three host-separator-sensitive ASAR read boundaries (copy-packaged-dependencies.cjs lines 35, 41, 99 and the two in verify-packaged-runtime-dependencies.cjs lines 39, 49). On POSIX, path.normalize is effectively a no-op on already-posix keys, so non-Windows behavior is unchanged. On Windows it converts the posix-normalized map keys into host-separator paths, matching @electron/asar's getNode() which splits on path.sep — directly addressing the two RED CI failures (missing dist/main/entry.js and node_modules/parent/index.js). Internal entries map, manifestAt key lookup, dependency traversal, additions, unpacked copy, and stream paths remain posix-keyed and untouched. The bare 'package.json' extract at line 91 needs no normalization (no separators). Tests assert against real archives with normalized host paths, not mocks, and preserve the real cross-spawn closure plus the unchanged packaged Electron import gate.

p2.note: The normalize-at-boundary pattern is now duplicated at five call sites with no shared helper; a future call site omitting path.normalize will reintroduce the same Windows-only failure class silently (asar.getNode returns null/throws only at runtime). Consider a tiny wrapper (e.g., asarHostPath(key)) in a shared module, or at least a comment at each site, to keep the invariant durable. Not blocking for this narrow delta.

info.link is re-derived with path.posix.relative from a posix key, which is correct, but it was already posix in the original archive listing; the mixed key-space (posix map keys, host paths only inside asar API arguments) relies on this convention implicitly. A short comment stating 'entries keys are always posix; only asar.* calls take host paths' would make the invariant auditable. Not blocking.

The real-closure test relies on symlinkSync(..., 'junction') for the dev node_modules link, which is Windows-appropriate but means the fixture exercises realpath resolution of a junction on Windows CI — good coverage, though the four RED tests reportedly failing are the archive-content assertions; once the normalize fix lands, the junction-based test also depends on the host Node resolving junctions inside import.meta.resolve from the archive probe, which the existing gate already covers on target CI. No change required; noting residual platform coupling.

limitations: Static review only: no execution, no ability to confirm the four Windows CI tests turn GREEN, only that the code change is the correct and minimal fix for the described path-separator defect.
Reviewer relied on the stated behavior of @electron/asar's getNode() splitting on path.sep from memory; the installed library version was not inspected.

Only the described packaging delta was in scope; the reviewer did not re-audit unchanged logic (dependency resolution, unpacked copy, rename/uncache atomicity) beyond confirming it is unmodified by this delta.
No source dependency, install, or authority changes were observed, consistent with the stated scope.
